scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor landscape of a winding dusty path beside a blue-green river, with olive trees, reeds, pale stones and small wildflowers. Golden slopes rise toward lavender hills beneath softly colored clouds. No people are visible.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The open path and river valley imaginatively evoke Jesus leaving Galilee and arriving in the regions of Judea beyond the Jordan after finishing his sayings. The landscape is not an exact reconstruction or a claim that he crossed the river here. Jesus remains outside the image; the trees, flowers and light are artistic setting details.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a smiling older man in teal and ochre standing with open hands amid a large crowd on a sunlit country path. A woman touches his arm, a bearded companion smiles beside him, and a wooden walking support rests on a folded mat beneath an olive tree. Hills and pale buildings recede behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The gathered crowd echoes the many who followed Jesus. The upright older man and unused walking support imaginatively suggest restoration through His healing; this particular man, ailment, and recovery scene are not specified in the verse. Jesus remains outside the frame. The people, clothing, landscape, and distant buildings are artistic conventions, not historical likenesses or archaeological claims.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed, bearded men stand on a sunlit stone path beneath an olive tree. The man in a rust-red mantle extends an open hand toward the left; his companions listen in green and brown mantles. A low stone wall, wildflowers, distant hills and village buildings surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The questioning gesture and watchful companions imaginatively depict the Pharisees testing Jesus about divorce for any cause. Jesus remains outside the frame. No wife or divorce is shown, since the verse records a question rather than a separation. The number of men, their appearance and the village setting are artistic choices, not historical likenesses or details specified by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two carved wooden figures, a bearded man and a long-haired woman in full-length garments, stand behind a blank parchment scroll on a limestone table. Olive branches, flowers, distant hills and a small village surround the sunlit garden.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative still life links the scroll to Jesus' appeal to what his hearers have read and the paired wooden figures to the Creator making humanity male and female from the beginning. The figures are visual teaching aids, not a literal creation scene or objects recorded in the verse; the garden and village are imagined. Neither Jesus nor the Creator is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a modestly dressed adult couple holding hands on a sunlit stone path. The man wears cream and brown; the woman wears terracotta and an ivory head covering. An open stone doorway stands behind them, with olive trees, wildflowers, a small house, and purple hills ahead.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative couple illustrates the marriage teaching rather than a recorded wedding. The doorway behind them suggests leaving the parental household; their joined hands and shared path toward a home suggest husband and wife beginning a united life. These visible signs point indirectly to becoming one flesh without depicting sexual intimacy. Their identities and setting are artistic conventions.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a cream tunic and brown mantle clasps hands with a woman in a green dress, rose shawl and linen head covering. They stand smiling beside an open wooden door in a sunlit stone courtyard, framed by an olive tree, flowers and a terracotta jar.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined husband and wife, their joined hands and shared home illustrate the unity of marriage and the command not to separate what God has joined. This illustrates Jesus' teaching, not a recorded wedding or an identified biblical couple. The courtyard, clothing and faces are imaginative; God and Jesus are not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two bearded men in cream tunics and green and rust-colored mantles stand beneath an olive tree on a rocky path. The younger man raises an open palm, and both look beyond the frame. Warm hills, olive groves and pale stone buildings recede behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The two men and their questioning gesture imaginatively represent those speaking to Jesus. Their faces, clothing and hillside setting are artistic choices, not details specified by this verse. Jesus remains out of view, and no divorce is enacted. Moses and the certificate are subjects of the question rather than figures or objects pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor garden with intertwined grapevine trunks around a wooden post, purple grapes and green leaves. A blank rolled parchment, loose cord and rough stone rest on a limestone table. Flowers, an olive tree, a low wall and distant hills surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This is an imaginative still life, not a recorded event. The blank scroll and untied cord suggest the permission to divorce, and the hard stone recalls hardness of heart. The living intertwined vines evoke the original marriage union contrasted with that concession. These objects are visual analogies, not objects named in the verse; neither Moses nor Jesus is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three clay cups rest on a sunlit wooden table in a stone courtyard. A pale cord joins two matching terracotta cups set apart, while a cream cup stands beside the right one. Folded striped linen, olive branches, a doorway, and distant hills complete the watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative still life reflects Jesus' warning about divorcing a wife and marrying another: two matching cups remain joined by a cord even as one stands beside a third. These objects are an illustration, not objects named in the verse or a historical marriage custom. The verse's exception for sexual immorality is retained in the explanation; no particular person's guilt is pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed men gather beneath an olive tree beside a stone path. A seated man in a rust-colored cloak raises an open hand toward the right; a gray-bearded companion rests a hand at his chin, and a younger man stands behind them. Wildflowers, golden hills and pale stone houses fill the sunlit landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The three men imaginatively represent disciples voicing the verse's conditional conclusion about marriage. Their questioning gesture and attentive faces turn toward Jesus outside the frame. No wife or wedding is shown because the marriage relationship is being discussed. The number of men, their appearances, clothing and olive-tree setting are artistic choices, not details supplied by this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed, bearded men sit on worn stone steps beneath an olive tree. The central man looks upward, the older man lowers his eyes, and the younger man rests a hand beneath his chin. Warm light falls across their garments, with wildflowers, hills, and pale buildings behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined listeners' receptive and pondering expressions suggest the difference between hearing a saying and being able to receive it. Jesus remains outside the image. The olive terrace, clothing, and gestures are artistic choices, not details supplied by the verse; their expressions do not identify who has or has not been given this capacity.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a cream tunic and brown mantle sits on a stone bench beneath an olive tree, looking upward with a gentle smile. A clay jug rests beside him; white flowers and a winding path lead through sunlit terraced hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The unnamed man alone in an olive garden is an imaginative meditation on freely foregoing marriage for the kingdom and receiving Jesus' teaching. The verse does not describe this man, garden or reflective pose; his appearance does not identify a bodily condition. No physical act is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of two women bringing three children beside a sunlit stone wall under an olive tree. One woman carries a toddler; the other holds a little girl's hand. Two robed men face them with raised palms and serious expressions. Pale houses and distant hills appear behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The caregivers and children imaginatively represent little ones being brought to Jesus for Him to lay His hands on them and pray. The two men with stopping gestures represent the disciples' rebuke. Jesus remains outside the frame. The exact people, clothing and setting are imaginative; the later welcome and blessing are not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three smiling children in ochre, terracotta and cream tunics walk rightward along a sunlit stone-lined path. The youngest reaches forward while an older child steadies a shoulder. A robed man stands aside at the left; olive branches, wildflowers and a distant village fill the watercolor setting.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The children's open path and eager approach imaginatively illustrate Jesus' command to allow them to come to Him without hindrance. He remains outside the picture to the right; the adult is an unnamed observer who leaves their way open. The setting, faces and clothes are artistic conventions, and no literal view of heaven is claimed.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two dark-haired children in earth-colored robes sit beneath an olive tree, looking up as two adult hands rest gently on their heads from outside the frame. Flowers grow beside the stone seat, and a sunlit path winds toward distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The hands resting on the children illustrate the laying on of hands; Jesus remains otherwise outside the frame. The winding path suggests His subsequent departure, rather than showing both actions simultaneously. The children's appearances, clothing, olive tree and rural setting are imaginative details, not details specified by this verse or claimed historical likenesses.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bearded man in a cream tunic and rust-colored mantle standing on a sunlit stone path, one palm open as he looks left. An olive tree and low stone wall frame him, with flowers, hills and a distant village behind.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The man's open hand and attentive gaze imagine the approach and question in Matthew 19:16. Jesus is understood to be outside the frame. The man, clothing and countryside are illustrative choices, not historical likenesses or a location stated by the verse; no answer or later episode is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A thoughtful young man in a cream tunic and rust-colored mantle sits beneath an olive tree, looking toward an open teaching hand at the left edge. Wildflowers surround the stone seat, and a sunlit path curves through olive groves toward distant hills and pale houses.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined setting presents the man listening to Jesus' reply, with Jesus outside the frame except for a teaching hand. His attentive posture reflects the call to keep the commandments; the living grove and path echo the desire to enter life. The verse does not specify the tree, landscape or clothing.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in an ivory robe and ochre mantle stands beneath an olive tree, raising an open palm and looking to the right. A sunlit stone path, low wall, wildflowers, olive groves and distant pale buildings fill the warm watercolor landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The questioning gesture and attentive gaze imaginatively frame the man asking which commandments Jesus means. Jesus remains outside the image. The olive grove, clothing and landscape are artistic conventions; the scene focuses on receiving His answer, whose prohibitions against murder, adultery, theft and false witness are explained in the verse note. It does not depict any of those forbidden acts.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of an adult man serving bread to an elderly woman beside an elderly man, while another man in blue sits with them at a shared courtyard table. Clay cups, bowls of food and olives sit beneath an olive tree beside a stone house.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined household meal illustrates both commands: an adult son's attentive service represents honoring his father and mother, and a neighbor sharing the same table and food represents loving one's neighbor as oneself. The verse states commands rather than describing this gathering; the people and courtyard are imaginative, and Jesus is not pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A young bearded man in a cream robe and ochre mantle stands beneath an olive tree, one hand at his chest and the other open toward the right. A sunlit stone path passes wildflowers and olive groves toward pale village houses and distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The hand at his chest evokes the young man's statement that he has kept all these things; his open palm and questioning expression evoke what he still lacks. He addresses Jesus beyond the frame. His appearance, clothing, path, olive tree and village are imaginative setting choices, not details specified in this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, open hands wait beside a wooden table holding an open leather purse, scattered coins, folded rust-colored cloth, and a bronze pitcher. An empty path winds through olive trees toward distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined arrangement sets possessions and a poor person's waiting hands beside an open path, illustrating Jesus' command to sell, give, and follow without claiming the listener obeyed. The open way evokes discipleship; the promised treasure in heaven is not pictured as material riches in the sky.
